newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cognac sales stagnate in 1996.
newsitem.headline: French cognac sales stagnate in 1996.

text.p: French sales of cognac stagnated in 1996, with a sharp rise in exports to the United States offset by a fall in exports to some Asian nations, the Cognac Marketing Board said on Saturday.

Total sales were the equivalent of 147.7 million bottles, exactly matching 1995 when exports were barely affected by foreign outrage at President Jacques Chirac's decision to stage a last round of six nuclear weapons tests in the South Pacific.

Export to the United States, the biggest market, expanded by 17.8 percent to 27.7 million bottles in 1996. Japan was stable in second place with 18.2 million bottles with Britain in third, up 2.5 percent at 12.1 million.
Among other markets, sales to Russia surged 115 percent to one million bottles. In France itself, sales gained 3.8 percent to 7.2 million bottles.

But cognac exports to Taiwan shrank by 27.4 percent, exports to Hong Kong slumped by 26 percent and Singapore's purchases tumbled by 18.9 percent. Sales to European nations including Italy and Switzerland also fell.
